docs.title: Welcome to Forge CLI
docs.text: Forge CLI is the "Linux for AI" - a next-generation open-source developer platform that acts as the central nervous system for AI agents.

docs.title: Why Forge?
docs.text: AI agents need more than just prompts. They need scheduling, long-running execution environments, memory, tools, and sandboxed plugins. Forge CLI provides a robust Microkernel architecture to manage all of these components seamlessly.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Microkernel Architecture: Event-driven buses routing actions efficiently.
  • Plugin Sandbox: Safely run untrusted 3rd-party plugins.
  • MCP Native: Out-of-the-box Model Context Protocol support.
  • Async Runtime: Parallel task execution, DAG scheduling, and Checkpointing.

Get started by navigating the sections on the left!

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Forge CLI is built as a Microkernel.

docs.title: The Kernel
docs.text: The kernel package acts as the central router for all system events and commands. It contains: - EventBus: Pub/Sub architecture for loosely coupled modules. - CommandBus: CQRS-style RPC for direct module-to-module requests. - PluginOrchestrator: Manages the lifecycle and sandboxing of all extensions.

docs.title: The Runtime
docs.text: The runtime executes Agents. It consists of: - TaskScheduler: A DAG-based async task graph. - WorkerPool: Manages parallel execution limits. - Checkpointing: State-saving to pause and resume workflows.

docs.title: Process Isolation
docs.text: In upcoming versions, Forge CLI will transition from importlib-based plugins to Wasm or IPC-isolated plugins for guaranteed memory safety.

docs.title: Command Line Interface (CLI)
docs.text: Forge uses Typer and Rich to provide a beautiful, modern terminal experience.

docs.title: forge init
docs.text: Initializes a new .forge workspace in the current directory.

docs.title: forge run
docs.text: Executes a specified Agent or Workflow. Usage: forge run <agent_name> --input "Hello"

docs.title: forge install
docs.text: Uses the Forge Package Manager to download and install a plugin. Usage: forge install mcp-github-server

docs.title: forge doctor
docs.text: Runs a diagnostic check on your environment, ensuring plugins load correctly and dependencies are met.

docs.title: Developer Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the Forge CLI core contributor guide!

docs.title: Setting up the Environment
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository.
  2. Install dependencies via Hatch or pip:
pip install -e .[dev]

docs.title: Code Quality Standards
docs.text:
We strictly enforce: - Ruff for linting and formatting. - Mypy for static type checking. - Pytest for testing (targeting 90% coverage). - Bandit/CodeQL for security scans.

Before submitting a Pull Request, run the pre-commit hooks:

pre-commit run --all-files

docs.title: Architecture Principles
docs.text: Ensure you read the Architecture Docs before modifying the kernel/ or runtime/ directories. We strictly adhere to SOLID principles and Dependency Injection.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Common patterns and code snippets for Forge CLI developers.

docs.title: Emitting an Event
docs.text:
from kernel.bus.events import EventBus

bus = EventBus()
await bus.publish("user.login", {"user_id": 123})

docs.title: Creating an MCP Client
docs.text:
from mcp.client import MCPClient

client = MCPClient("node server.js")
client.connect()
tools = client.discover_tools()

docs.title: Plugin Documentation
docs.text: Everything in Forge is a plugin. If you want to extend the Kernel, you build a plugin.

docs.title: The IPlugin Interface
docs.text:
Every plugin must implement the IPlugin interface from the Forge SDK:

from forge_cli.sdk.plugin import IPlugin, PluginContext

class MyPlugin(IPlugin):
    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "my_plugin"

    @property
    def version(self) -> str:
        return "1.0.0"

    async def on_load(self, context: PluginContext) -> None:
        print("Plugin loaded!")

docs.title: Sandboxing
docs.text: Plugins are executed in isolation. Direct access to host memory or file systems outside the designated .forge/workspace will result in a PermissionDeniedError.

docs.title: SDK Reference
docs.text: The forge_cli.sdk package exposes all the tools necessary for developers to build extensions, agents, and orchestrators.

docs.title: sdk.agent
docs.text: Contains the Agent base class for defining AI behaviors.

docs.title: sdk.tool
docs.text: Decorators and classes for exposing Python functions to LLMs.

docs.title: sdk.llm
docs.text: Standardized interfaces (ILLMProvider) ensuring Forge is model-agnostic. Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, etc.

docs.title: sdk.memory
docs.text: Short-term (MemoryWindow) and long-term (VectorStore) memory abstractions.

docs.title: User Documentation
docs.text: This section is for end-users who want to install Forge CLI and run pre-built agents or plugins.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install forge-cli

docs.title: Basic Concepts
docs.text:
• Workspace: Your .forge/ directory containing configurations, memory, and local plugins.
  • Agent: An autonomous entity running in the runtime.
  • Tool: An MCP or native python function exposed to agents.

docs.title: Common Commands
docs.text:
• forge init: Initializes a workspace in the current directory.
  • forge install <package>: Installs a Forge extension from the registry.
  • forge run <agent>: Spawns an agent in the runtime.
